correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the two pure-death populations: while part majorities oppose, only originally misaligned spin groups update, with rates i and j from independent rate-one clocks. Reversing the order under x=e^{-tau} gives independent Beta(u+1,a-u) and Beta(v+1,b-v) variables. Integrating the binomial CDF yields the stated finite beta sum; reflection symmetry gives probability 1/2 for a=m,b=n. The beta-order-statistic CLT, with variance (2p-1)/p in time, and n/m->kappa give Phi(delta/sqrt(p(2p-1)(1+1/kappa))). Boundary p=1 remains nondegenerate. A sample K31,101 initially has a global negative majority yet P(positive)≈0.9786857. Independent rational state-recursion checks covered 196 (m,n,a,b) combinations and 16 symmetry cases.
residual_risks: Only odd parts and strictly opposing part majorities; no tie rule, heterogeneous rate, positive-temperature or absorption-time conclusion.
Order-statistic wording in proof calls Beta(u+1,a-u) an (u+1)-st largest uniform; the beta parameter and CDF formula are correct but this particular order-direction label should say smallest.
Finite enumerations corroborate and do not prove the Gaussian limit.

value.rationale: Opposed part-majorities are a natural kinetic-Ising conflict. Exact finite-size phase-selection probabilities, unequal-size perfect-polarization symmetry, sharp central-limit crossover and asymptotic reversal of the global initial majority identify qualitative consequences not obtainable merely from a standard ferromagnetic attractor argument.
residual_risks: No broader empirical or arbitrarily weighted graph generalization is supported.

final_claim: Exact independent-beta threshold race for opposed strict majorities in zero-temperature K_(m,n) Glauber dynamics; equal fully opposed sides give probability 1/2 even at unequal sizes; fixed-ratio polarization thresholds and a Gaussian window distinguish part from global majority.
limitations: Odd part sizes at least three and initial strict opposed majorities; endpoints with ties excluded.
One ambiguous order-statistic description is a harmless nomenclature issue; all stated Beta parameters and formulas consistent.
Historical alternative pure-death formulation cannot be completely excluded.
